g.text: Decision D3 · Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper logic (connect D2)?
decision-code-D3 · generated from code.json · confidence medium

svg.text: Rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Chosen: B. Reason of the orchestrator: the wrapper is the profile made real (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping), and the scrub needs 1 owner. Process group and kill go through the platform interface, which each context calls. This differs from the recommendation of this step. The step recommended C: Recommended option C. Strongest argument against it: fleet-runtime then owns 4 process roles and the team has
Would flip if: The wrapper holds lease logic
Would flip if: The CLI event map turns out to need task state

g.text: task-execution: the wrapper writes heartbeat.json and exit.json, which are task-execution facts.
+ The files it writes feed the lease and the stall ladder
− task-execution would start processes, against connect N3
! The process-group and sandbox code leaks into a core context
worker-profiles: the wrapper builds the private config home and maps CLI events per
+ Per-CLI event mapping sits with the harness adapters
− worker-profiles would own a process role and the 256k context guard at run time
leaf crate, no contextleaf crate, no context
fleet-runtime: the wrapper is a process role of the binary, like fleetd and fleetd check; it asks worker-profiles for the CLI event map.
+ Process groups, the platform layer and atomic file writes already live there
+ Keeps both core contexts free of process code
− fleet-runtime is already the largest supporting context
! The CLI event map crosses from worker-profiles at run time
